title: Untangle / Two checkout knots untied
scope: Six runtime files in the before fixture and five after: checkout, price quotes, and pending-order reconciliation.

knots.title: Callers encode and decode stored JSON
knots.evidence: Before, place_order assembles and serializes the order, while pending_orders decodes raw rows passed through read_raw_order_history in history.py and _rows_for_reconciliation in orders.py. After, InMemoryStorage.write_order and read_orders own encoding and decoding. Shared checks confirm the same callable outputs, stored bytes, key order, errors, read order, and validation effects for this fixture. The price-lookup detour is recorded as knot #2.
knots.remedy: Give the storage owner write_order and read_orders operations; remove history.py's read_raw_order_history pass-through and orders.py's _rows_for_reconciliation facade as callers hand JSON ownership to storage, while preserving the raw row APIs and serialized format.

before.summary: Orders serializes records to JSON bytes. Reconciliation decodes those bytes after they pass through history.py's read_raw_order_history helper and orders.py's _rows_for_reconciliation facade.

snippets.code:
def read_raw_order_history(storage: object) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
    return storage.read_all()

after.summary: Orders sends records to storage; reconciliation receives decoded records. Storage owns both JSON operations.

snippets.code:
def write_order(self, order: dict[str, object]) -> bytes:
        raw = json.dumps(order, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
        self.append(raw)
        return raw

comparison.benefit: Removing the history and order forwarding helpers leaves storage as the sole JSON-format owner. A format change can be handled there instead of being repeated across callers.
comparison.preserved: For this InMemoryStorage fixture, shared tests check the callable outputs, stored bytes and key order, validation errors, operation order, pending-order filtering, and reads in both snapshots.

verification.note: Runs the same seven behavior tests in separate processes against before and after. Verified with Python 3.14.10.

knots.title: Price quotes detour through orders and storage
knots.evidence: Before, quote imports an order helper at runtime. That helper forwards the product ID to storage, which delegates to catalog.price_for. The quote feature crosses order-creation and storage code for a catalog lookup. After, quote calls catalog.price_for directly. Shared checks preserve the same quote results, errors, order outputs, stored bytes, and storage-operation order.
knots.remedy: Have quote call catalog.price_for directly and remove the price-forwarding helpers from orders.py and storage.py.

before.summary: Quote sends the product ID through an order helper and a storage helper before catalog lookup.

after.summary: Quote passes the product ID directly to catalog.price_for.

comparison.benefit: The pricing feature no longer crosses order-creation or storage code to read a catalog price.
comparison.preserved: Shared tests check quote output and validation errors, plus order output, exact stored bytes, key order, operation order, and reconciliation behavior in both snapshots.

verification.note: Runs the same seven behavior tests in separate processes against before and after. Verified with Python 3.14.10.
Compiles all before and after runtime files in memory and imports them through the isolated behavior checks. Verified with Python 3.14.10.

before.coverage: Synthetic fixture baseline. Checkout, price-quote, and reconciliation entry points are traced across all six before runtime files. The quote price path crosses quotes.py, orders.py, storage.py, and catalog.py. Reconciliation reaches storage through the orders.py facade and history.py pass-through. The fixture has no separate runtime configuration, database, web framework, or deployment path.

place_order validates and calculates the order through quote.
storage resolves the price on checkout's quote path.
place_order appends the JSON bytes through the raw storage API.
quote is the price-quote entry point.

_order_unit_price forwards the product ID to storage.

pending_total is the reconciliation entry point.
pending_orders requests raw rows through the order facade.

after.coverage: Synthetic fixture final snapshot. The same three entry points and five runtime files are traced. Quote reads prices directly from catalog.py, and storage owns JSON encoding and decoding. The fixture has no separate runtime configuration, database, web framework, or deployment path.
